correctness.rationale: Set G(x)=xL(x), H(x)=x^pL(x^p). De Bruijn conjugacy gives G(b_n^p)~n and n/b_n²→0 since p<2. Under eventual almost increase, Potter lower bounds H(x)/H(b_n) for x≤b_n by (x/b_n)^(p+eta), eta in (0,2-p), controlling the below-b_n variance using Cesàro UI, Doob L² and Jensen. Above b_n, L(b_n^p)<=K L(|X|^p) bounds the pth tail moment and von Bahr–Esseen plus maximal inequalities (triangle bound p=1) give mean convergence. If no almost increase, select u_m<v_m with L(u_m)/L(v_m)>=m³, n_m=floor(G(u_m)), and Bernoulli-signed spikes ±v_m^(1/p) at probability q_m=1/(mG(v_m)); every special row is iid and other rows zero. Cesàro UI is ≤1/m in late special rows, probability of any spike is O(1/m), while expected pth maximal deviation on the one-spike event is asymptotic to L(u_m)/(m L(v_m))>=m²; force distinct n_m as in proof. The explicit oscillating L is slowly varying because its log-derivative in log x tends to zero while peak/trough ratio diverges. Independent sampled asymptotic spike-ratio checks corroborate but do not prove infinite statements.

originality.rationale: A 2022 weak law posed an Lp upgrade question. The 2024 Thành primary paper affirmatively answers the increasing L>=1 case and proves per-array sufficient/necessary tail conditions, as well as a particular decreasing-weight counterexample. The final claim is different: a universal all-slowly-varying-weight iff characterization via eventual almost increase, with a sparse counterexample for every violating L, including weights >=1. The earlier sufficient theorem and its isolated example do not imply this functional necessity. The Oxford-authorized text retrieval supplied primary pages 1-9, including Theorem 3.1; a further read request was safety-blocked and not retried, leaving unseen later sections as a residual risk.
residual_risks: Complete publisher article beyond page 9 was not read; a subsequent authorized pagination call was safety-blocked, not retried. This access uncertainty alone does not refute a positive best-of-knowledge assessment.
An older Orlicz/quasi-monotone weight theorem might imply this exact universal characterization under different terminology.

value.rationale: This identifies the precise functional boundary at which a natural Cesàro-UI weak-law assumption upgrades universally to p-mean maximal convergence. The necessity construction systematically separates probability convergence from mean convergence even for weights bounded below by one, while the sufficiency extends beyond monotone weights. It directly addresses the mathematical scope of an existing published question and later partial affirmative theorem.
residual_risks: Scope is universal across arrays, not a decision rule for an individual array.

final_claim: For 1<=p<2 and locally bounded positive slowly varying L, Cesàro UI of |X|^p L(|X|^p) implies maximal normalized p-mean convergence for every rowwise independent triangular array, with b_n=(n L-tilde(n))^(1/p), if and only if L is eventually almost increasing. If that functional property fails, symmetric iid-within-row three-point arrays meet the same Cesàro UI and weak law but have limsup expected normalized maximal pth moment infinite. An explicit slowly varying L>=1 exhibits this failure.
limitations: 1<=p<2, positive slowly varying L with compact local bounds, independent within each row.
Counterexample distributions vary between sparse rows.
